question: How can successive provider capture versions retain exactly what was observed at retrieval time, separately from bar timestamps, so snapshot lifecycle comparisons do not claim that later-captured OHLC was available historically?
reason: This replay resolves deterministic rebuild, non-rescue and replacement reporting, but cannot establish historical value availability from a single later capture. Repeating unchanged-corpus cutoffs cannot supply that evidence.
scope: Design a bounded append-only capture/version and availability-provenance contract using existing observation transports where sufficient. Preserve actual retrieval timestamps and values; distinguish recorded bar timestamp, capture availability, geometric eligibility and Elliott completion. No invented bar-close calendar, no change to P005 eligibility, no forced persistent endpoints.
